expectations.name: llm_judge(The response is a structured c, threshold=0.6)
expectations.message: The answer is a structured, severity-prioritized code review that concretely identifies the swallowed payment exception, silent mailer failure, oversized multi-responsibility method, parameter/return issues, logging problems, and missing tests, with actionable fixes and a clear next-steps list.

writing.overall_comment: This is a strong, well-bounded reviewer definition; trimming checklist length and adding concrete routing triggers would improve delegation efficiency.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: The description clearly identifies code review expertise and invocation purpose, though it could name concrete triggers such as PR or diff reviews.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: The role, review process, checklist, and structured feedback format are explicit, with only minor ambiguity around the Semantic tool and skill declarations.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: The agent is explicitly review-only, forbids edits, commits, and refactors, and defines clear hand-back cases for implementation, ADR-level decisions, and missing context.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: The prompt is well organized but quite long, with extensive checklist and language-specific notes that may exceed an ideal token budget for a single-purpose review subagent.

suggestions: In the review subagent's prompt, trim the extensive checklist to only the highest-priority review criteria and remove redundant items to reduce token count.
In the review subagent's prompt, move language-specific notes out of the main instructions into an optional appendix or conditional reference so they are included only when relevant.
In the review subagent's prompt, add a target token/length limit for the instructions and verify the final prompt stays within it.
